predecessors.name: Twenty-third Dynasty of Egypt
predecessors.text: Thebes and Upper Egypt up to Herakleopolis, the lands the Piye page says his authority reached after his campaign (Thebes, the western oases and Herakleopolis)

predecessors.name: Twenty-fourth Dynasty of Egypt
predecessors.text: Sais, the western Delta and Memphis, taken by Shebitku "around 712 BC" (25th Dynasty page)

predecessors.name: Twenty-second Dynasty of Egypt
predecessors.text: the eastern Delta around Tanis, where Osorkon IV and the other Delta kings submitted to Piye

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Kush
predecessors.text: The Napatan kingdom whose kings became pharaohs; its Nubian land stays with kingdom-of-kush, this dossier covers the Egyptian realm only

successors.name: Assyrian Egypt
successors.text: Thebes and Upper Egypt, which "peacefully submitted itself to Psamtik's fleet in 656 BC"

successors.name: Kingdom of Kush
successors.text: "The 25th Dynasty ended with its rulers retreating to their spiritual homeland at Napata"

ledger.x: 754: the Kushite Twenty-fifth Dynasty is established, with its reach at Thebes.
728: Piye holds Upper Egypt to Herakleopolis.
728: the Delta kings submit to Piye.
728: Piye sails south and goes home to Nubia, "never to return to Egypt"; the fighting of his campaign ends and the Delta kings are left to rule.
712: Shebitku brings the whole Nile Valley under direct Kushite rule.
712: the Delta kings cease to be vassals when Shebitku takes the Delta directly (see the gain above).
712: the Kushite court moves its Egyptian capital to Memphis.
671: Memphis falls to Esarhaddon and Taharqa flees south.
667: Ashurbanipal drives Taharqa out of the north.
663: Thebes is sacked and the north is lost for good.
663: the Assyrian war ends in an Assyrian victory; Kushite authority in Upper Egypt persisted until 656.
656: Psamtik I takes Thebes without a fight.
656: the Kushite dynasty ends in Egypt.

wars.name: Piye's invasion of Egypt
wars.outcome: Piye won at Herakleopolis, took Hermopolis and Memphis and received the submission of the Delta kings, then returned to Nubia without garrisoning the Delta.

wars.name: Shebitku's conquest of the Delta
wars.outcome: Shebitku took Sais, captured Bakenranef and ruled the whole valley; the capital moved to Memphis.

wars.name: Assyrian conquest of Egypt
wars.outcome: Assyrian victory: Esarhaddon took Memphis in 671, Taharqa returned in 669, Ashurbanipal drove him to Thebes in 667, Tantamani's return of 664/663 ended with the sack of Thebes; Psamtik I, the Assyrian vassal, unified the north.

wars.name: Sennacherib's campaign in Judah (Eltekeh)
wars.outcome: Taharqa's army aided Hezekiah; it was "beaten at Eltekeh", though the page says it "could be interpreted as a victory for the double kingdom".

wars.name: Revolt of Ashdod
wars.outcome: The page says Shabaka backed an uprising at Ashdod, which Sargon II defeated; the rebel Iamani was extradited to Assyria in 712.

certainty.note: The pages name cities and rulers, not frontiers; the Delta kings and Memphis change hands several times.
